stem: A lung recipient calls the transplant clinic reporting new shortness of breath. According to urgent-contact education, how should the coordinator classify this symptom?

options.text: An urgent matter requiring prompt transplant team contact
A non-urgent matter appropriate for the next routine medication refill call
A symptom that never requires notification after transplant
A reason to stop all immunosuppression without medical guidance

explanation.rationale_correct: Shortness of breath is listed among urgent matters requiring prompt transplant team contact, alongside infection symptoms, rejection signs, chest pain, and bleeding.

rationale_incorrect.B: Shortness of breath is explicitly urgent, not a routine refill matter.
rationale_incorrect.C: Post-transplant teaching requires reporting shortness of breath to the team.
rationale_incorrect.D: Urgent symptoms prompt team contact and evaluation, not unilateral immunosuppression cessation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → h. Communication → iii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Urgent matters may include … Shortness of breath

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → h. Communication with the transplant team → iii. Urgent matters (shortness of breath listed); PDF p. 111 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 030700 item; lung urgent-contact angle distinct from chest pain (cctc-3029), rectal bleeding (cctc-3022), stroke FAST (cctc-3017), and infection (cctc-3002); anchor verified on Cupples p. 111.

stem: A kidney recipient one week post-transplant has unexplained fever, abdominal pain, decreased urinary output, and a rising serum creatinine. Which abnormality pattern is MOST consistent with a urinary leak complication?

options.text: Fever, pain, oliguria, elevated creatinine, and possible wound drainage together
Stable creatinine with increased urine output and no pain
Isolated mild postoperative fatigue without laboratory changes
Normal graft function with only routine incision healing

explanation.rationale_correct: Urinary leak at the ureterovesical anastomosis may present with unexplained fever, abdominal pain, decreased urinary output, elevated creatinine, and wound drainage.

rationale_incorrect.B: Urinary leak typically decreases output and elevates creatinine rather than increasing output with stable creatinine.
rationale_incorrect.C: Isolated fatigue without laboratory or output changes does not match urinary leak presentation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Normal graft function without symptoms contradicts the fever, pain, oliguria, and creatinine rise described.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 17, Kidney Transplantation → h. Urinary leak → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Unexplained fever … Decreased urinary output … Elevated creatinine … Wound drainage

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 17 → h. Urinary leak → ii. Clinical signs (fever, pain, decreased output, elevated creatinine, wound drainage); PDF p. 903 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 030100 item; kidney urinary-leak lab pattern distinct from liver LFT monitoring (cctc-3025); anchor verified on Cupples p. 903.

stem: A kidney recipient is diagnosed with a urinary leak at the ureterovesical anastomosis. What initial management approach is MOST appropriate for a minor leak?

options.text: Permanent cessation of all immunosuppression without surgical input
No intervention because urinary leaks never occur after kidney transplant
Immediate graft nephrectomy for every minor leak without trial of conservative management

explanation.rationale_correct: Urinary leaks at the ureterovesical anastomosis are treated with long-term indwelling urinary catheters or surgical intervention for minor leaks, depending on severity.

rationale_incorrect.B: Management focuses on drainage or surgical repair, not unilateral immunosuppression cessation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Urinary leak is a recognized post-transplant complication at the ureterovesical anastomosis.
rationale_incorrect.D: Minor leaks may be managed conservatively with catheter drainage before considering more invasive options.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 17, Kidney Transplantation → h. Urinary leak → iii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Urine leaks are treated with long-term indwelling urinary catheters, or surgical intervention for minor leaks

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 17 → h. Urinary leak → iii. Treatment (indwelling catheter or surgical intervention for minor leaks); PDF p. 903 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 030200 item; kidney urinary-leak management angle distinct from rejection fever mechanism (cctc-3026); anchor verified on Cupples p. 903.

stem: After a transplant program registers a new waitlist candidate in UNet, when must the program submit the Transplant Candidate Registration (TCR) form to meet OPTN timely data requirements?

options.text: Within 90 days after registering the candidate on the waiting list
Only after the recipient's five-year transplant anniversary
Within 1 day of every routine clinic medication refill
Never; TCR submission is optional for transplant hospitals

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN Policy 18.1 requires transplant hospitals to submit the Transplant Candidate Registration (TCR) within 90 days after registering the candidate on the waiting list.

rationale_incorrect.B: TCR is required early after waitlist registration, not only at five years post-transplant.
rationale_incorrect.C: Routine medication refills are not the TCR submission trigger.
rationale_incorrect.D: TCR is a required timely data instrument for registered waitlist candidates.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: 90 days after the transplant hospital registers the candidate on the waiting list

references.locator: Policy 18.1 → Data Submission Requirements (Transplant Candidate Registration [TCR] within 90 days after waitlist registration); PDF p. 332 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fourth 030800 item; TCR timing distinct from TRR (cctc-3027), UNet registration fields (cctc-3019), and SRTR aggregation (cctc-3005); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 332.
